versions.releaseNotes:
v2.3.0 — Subtitles everywhere + watch history that works

 Online subtitle search built into the player — search by title, pick a release, and it loads straight into playback (desktop mpv and the browser player, streaming sources included)
 Watch progress now saves on desktop direct playback — Continue Watching and History finally record in the desktop app, and the web player saves progress too
 Smart resume: per-episode resume points for TV, the correct position across source and episode switches, and a fresh start when auto-advancing to the next episode
 Faster playback start: mpv pre-warms from the detail page, and direct sources fail over in ~200 ms through a two-provider pipeline with chain prefetch
 New home feed with lazy-loaded trailers, phone-parity movie/TV detail pages, unified search palette (Ctrl+K), and a rebuilt watch page with a tabbed Episodes/Sources hub
 Downloads hub: HDHub download pages, title-based file names, metadata badges, TV episode grouping
 New providers: JustAnime (anime), Way2Movies, MovieBox and Bing with per-platform availability flags; Falix migrated to its new host and files API

Fixes:
 Fixed the stuck "Preparing Stream" loader — mpv events now reach the player before overlay side effects run
 mpv is auto-downloaded and SHA-256 verified at build time, so an installer can no longer ship without the playback engine
 Branded error page with retry when the app's own content fails to load, instead of a blank window
 Subtitles no longer sit too high over the video

Under the hood:
- Routine debug console output silenced in production builds
- Path-form deep links (/movie/{id}) redirect correctly on web; the desktop static export excludes server API routes by design
- Theme tokens recalibrated (OKLCH) for consistent contrast across pages

v2.2.0 — Native playback engine + smarter sources

 Direct sources now play in a native mpv engine — MKV, HEVC and AV1 play without transcoding, with hardware decoding and fast seeking
 Source health you can trust: every source is byte-validated before you click it (no more green links that fail to play), and a source that fails during playback turns red and sinks to the bottom of the picker
 Automatic failover that actually works: if a source dies, the player walks ranked alternatives and remembers the last source that worked for next time
 Visible Audio and Subtitle buttons on the player with online subtitle search, plus a preferred audio language setting
 If every direct source dies, the app falls back to the web embed automatically instead of a dead-end error
 Instant watch pages: continue-watching titles, the next episode and top sources are prefetched in the background
 Window-level fullscreen on the player, first-run language prompt, and the source picker now shows the auto-pick reason and verified counts

Fixes:
 Ad-blocking is now guaranteed active on embed servers — a debug-logging listener could silently replace the filter engine and let ads through

v2.1.0 — Faster watch page, redesigned Continue Watching, bug fixes

 Watch page loads instantly — embed URL computed from URL params before TMDB resolves, webview mounts immediately
 Continue Watching cards redesigned — 16:9 backdrops, always-visible play button, episode pill badges, gold progress bar (matches mobile app)
 Hero and card ratings now show 0-10 scale everywhere
 Falix backend migrated to dl.falixmovies.com

Bug fixes:
 Fixed React error #185 on history page (useSyncExternalStore snapshot mismatch)
 Fixed HomeModeFeed crash when query data is undefined
 Fixed Falix download page returning 'Missing required query parameter' (static export prerender issue)

Under the hood:
- Route restructuring: detail/watch/download/person pages migrated from path params to query params for static export compatibility
- Hover-prefetch on Watch Now buttons (movie/tv detail pages)
- TV season short-circuits when ?season= already in URL

v2.0.0 — Desktop app release

Falix downloads fixed (dead host replaced with the live backend)
Working download speed limiter (Balanced / Slower caps) — now real pause/resume pacing, previously a silent no-op, and synced between Settings and Downloads
Clear Watch History now asks for confirmation before wiping
Carousels swipe correctly on mouse drag (no more accidental card selection)
Anime home feed with a movie/TV / anime mode toggle
Rewritten Transparency, Privacy and Legal pages (GPL-3.0, /how-it-works renamed to /transparency)
Player and desktop-shell improvements: secure webview, episode sidebar, mobile episode sheet, audio toggle, playback recorder
v1.0.4 — Desktop watch-security hardening + Screenscape ad-suppression, no-rebuild config prep

v1.0.3 — Reliable ad-blocking for provider playback

Security — the fix you'll actually feel:
Ad-blocking now holds through the Play click. Previously, ads reappeared right when the provider's video started playing. Root cause: the in-page protection relied on a CDP-injected script that died the moment the provider navigated cross-site (the Play action swaps the renderer process).

Replaced with a session-level preload that runs at document-start in every frame, re-applies itself in each new renderer process, and cannot be removed by the page. Canvas/WebGL fingerprinting spoofed, crypto-miners and background workers blocked, tracking beacons and storage keys filtered, and ad-container elements hidden.

CDP is now a verification layer only — it confirms protections are active in every live frame and logs loudly if anything is missing.

Bug fixes:
Removed a full-width dark overlay that appeared over the top of Server 1's player (plus a smaller stray overlay on Server 6). These were band-aid divs never intended for Server 1 — the player area is now clean.

Under the hood:
Fixed a post-build step so the shared security package resolves correctly at runtime (this is what let the preload load). Removed dead code (old video-window path, legacy protection scripts, a stale backup file).

What's Changed:
StreamGuide custom video player with seek optimization
Smoother video controls and enhanced playback experience
Performance improvements and bug fixes
Bug fixes: removed native menu bar, fixed missing CSS styling, custom app icon, and auto-update support.

Initial desktop release. Browse movies and TV shows with the same great FilmSnaps experience — now native on desktop. Secure video player window with 6-layer security protection: ad blocking, popup blocking, navigation guards, session isolation, and resource monitoring.
